content.overview: Two young children run hand in hand along a path beside a playground in a green park. They are smiling at each other, with slides, benches, flowers, trees, and a fountain in the background.

evidence.label: People
evidence.detail: Two children are the clear foreground subjects. Several distant park visitors/adults appear in the background, but they are too small for reliable identity or relationship claims.

evidence.label: Child — left
evidence.detail: Young boy with medium brown hair; bright blue short-sleeved T-shirt, beige/tan shorts, and dark athletic shoes. He extends his free arm outward while running and looks toward the other child.

evidence.label: Child — right
evidence.detail: Young girl with light brown/blonde hair in two braids tied with red bows; sleeveless yellow dress with pale trim; white shoes. She smiles toward the child beside her while running.

evidence.label: Foreground
evidence.detail: Green lawn and a tan gravel/mulch path. The children are mid-stride with one foot lifted, showing active motion.

evidence.label: Middle ground
evidence.detail: Large playground structure with green slides, tan support posts, and a dark green roof; benches and a flower border behind it.

evidence.label: Background
evidence.detail: Mature leafy trees, several blurred visitors, and a white fountain spray on the right.

evidence.label: Weather / light
evidence.detail: Bright sunlight enters from the upper left. Green grass and leafy trees surround the playground.

evidence.label: Action / body language
evidence.detail: The children are running together while holding hands. Both are smiling and turning slightly toward one another.

evidence.label: Colors / textures
evidence.detail: Vivid green grass and trees, yellow dress, blue shirt, dark green playground, orange/yellow/pink flowers, white fountain spray.

evidence.label: Composition
evidence.detail: The running children dominate the lower center, while the playground frames the activity and gives the scene a clear childhood setting.

micro: The children’s joined hands are a strong familiarity cue, but they do not prove exact kinship.
Both children are captured mid-stride, with swinging arms and lifted feet, creating clear present-continuous action language.

inference.medium: The children may be siblings, close friends, cousins, or classmates. Holding hands while running and looking toward each other suggests familiarity, but exact kinship is not visible.
inference.low: They might be racing toward another activity, moving from the playground to the fountain, or simply running for fun. The destination is not visible.

content.guardrail: Visible running, hand-holding, smiles, clothing, playground, and park details are facts. Sibling, friend, cousin, or classmate readings may be discussed as supported possibilities; exact kinship, exact ages, and any link between distant adults and the children remain unproven.

They may be siblings or friends, and one of them may have challenged the other to hurry. The relationship and conversation are imagined; the running, hand-holding, and smiles are visible.

grammar.title: USED TO AND WOULD FOR PAST HABITS AND CHILDHOOD MEMORIES
grammar.explainer: Use used to / would for childhood habits when speaking about memories beyond the photo: We used to play in the park after school. Do not turn an imagined past habit into a claim about the photographed children.
examples: We used to play in the park after school.
When I was a child, we would run around the playground after class.

models.A1–A2: Two children are running in a park. They are holding hands and smiling. One child is wearing a blue shirt and shorts, and the other is wearing a yellow dress. A playground is behind them. The day looks sunny and warm.
models.B1–B2: Two young children are running hand in hand along a park path in front of a playground. The child on the left wears a bright blue T-shirt and tan shorts, while the child on the right wears a yellow dress and white shoes with red bows in her braids. Both are smiling and looking toward each other. Green trees, colorful flowers, and a fountain make the park feel bright and lively.
models.C1–C2: The photograph freezes a high-energy moment of shared childhood play. The two children move in step while holding hands, their smiles and sideways glances showing that the pleasure comes as much from doing the activity together as from running itself. Their vivid blue and yellow clothing stands out against the saturated greens of the park, while the playground structure and fountain establish a clear recreational setting. Visually, the most defensible conclusion is that they are two children with an easy, playful familiarity.

speaking.30: Give 4–5 simple sentences from visible evidence: setting + three visible facts + one action. If you use used to or would, make it clearly about your own childhood memory, not the children in the photo.
speaking.60: Rebuild the scene in a clear order. Use at least two lesson phrases — “run hand in hand” and “playground structure” — then add one cautious inference with seems, may, might, or could.
speaking.90: Speak without reading: overview → key subject details → environment/weather/light → action → atmosphere → one Before/Now/Next link. Finish by separating one visible fact from one inference.

listener.label: Park Listener
listener.sub: Help a listener reconstruct the playground scene from concrete, connected details.

prompts.label: OPEN THE SCENE
prompts.prompt: Give me one clear opening sentence: who is in the foreground, where are they, and what are they doing?
prompts.hint: Start with two children + park/playground + running hand in hand.

prompts.label: ADD APPEARANCE
prompts.prompt: Add two visible clothing or appearance details that help me distinguish the two children.
prompts.hint: Try blue T-shirt, tan shorts, yellow dress, braids, or red bows.

prompts.label: PLACE THE BACKGROUND
prompts.prompt: Where are the playground structure, slides, flower border, benches, and fountain relative to the children?
prompts.hint: Use behind, in the background, on the left, or on the right.

prompts.label: DESCRIBE THE ACTION
prompts.prompt: What are the two children doing right now? Use action language that fits the still image.
prompts.hint: Try are running / are holding hands / are smiling.

prompts.label: RECONSTRUCT THE FRAME
prompts.prompt: Now give me a short connected description that would let someone rebuild the main park scene without seeing the photo.
prompts.hint: Combine people, action, clothing, path, playground, and one background detail.

detective.label: Park Detective
detective.sub: Separate visible play from title context, cautious relationship inference, and unsupported family claims.

prompts.label: VISIBLE FACT
prompts.prompt: State two facts that are directly visible in the park scene.
prompts.hint: Use action, clothing, playground, path, fountain, or flowers.

prompts.label: ONE SUPPORTED INFERENCE
prompts.prompt: Give one cautious inference about the interaction and name the visible clue that supports it.
prompts.hint: Use seem / appear / may, then mention hand-holding, smiles, or mutual gaze.

prompts.label: TITLE VS PHOTO
prompts.prompt: What does the photograph directly prove about the children, and what relationship details remain uncertain?
prompts.hint: The photo proves two children are playing closely together, not kinship.

prompts.label: DRAW THE GUARDRAIL
prompts.prompt: Name one claim about exact age, parentage, supervision, or destination that the image cannot prove.
prompts.hint: Exact ages and the distant adults’ relationship are unknown.

prompts.label: REPAIR CERTAINTY
prompts.prompt: Repair this idea into evidence-safe English: “Those adults are their parents.”
prompts.hint: Say that distant adults are visible but cannot be linked reliably to the children.

story.label: Playground Story Relay
story.sub: Extend Before → Now → Next while keeping imagined park events clearly hypothetical.

prompts.label: START WITH NOW
prompts.prompt: Begin with the visible present moment on the park path.
prompts.hint: Use are running / are holding hands / are smiling.

prompts.label: STEP BACK
prompts.prompt: What may have happened shortly before this moment?
prompts.hint: They may have been using the playground equipment or playing on the grass.

prompts.label: MOVE FORWARD
prompts.prompt: What might happen next if the scene continues naturally?
prompts.hint: They might continue to another part of the playground or stop near the fountain.

prompts.label: TIE STORY TO A CLUE
prompts.prompt: Which visible detail makes your story extension plausible?
prompts.hint: Use the playground, path, fountain, hand-holding, or smiles.

prompts.label: THREE-SENTENCE RELAY
prompts.prompt: Retell the moment as Before → Now → Next in three connected sentences, keeping Before and Next cautious.
prompts.hint: Before they may have… Now they are… Next they might…

recasts.overview: I first notice two young children running hand in hand along a path beside a playground in a green park.
recasts.detail: The child on the left wears a bright blue T-shirt and tan shorts, while the child on the right wears a yellow dress with red bows in her braids.
recasts.spatial: The children dominate the foreground; the playground structure and slides are behind them, with flowers, benches, trees, and a fountain farther back.
recasts.action: Both children are running, holding hands, smiling, and turning slightly toward each other.
recasts.inference: Their joined hands, smiles, and mutual attention suggest easy familiarity, although the photograph alone does not prove that they are siblings.
recasts.timeline: Before this moment, they may have been using the playground; now they are running together, and next they might continue toward another part of the park.
recasts.extension: The scene feels energetic and cooperative because the children are running hand in hand and smiling, but their exact ages, family relationship, and destination remain unknown.

models.title: A fall that ended the game

A1.text: I once fell while running in a park. I cried, but later I played again.

A2.text: One time I fell on a path while running. My knee hurt, and I was upset, but after a rest I went back to playing.

B1.text: Not every park memory is perfect. I once fell while running, scraped my knee, and spent several minutes feeling sorry for myself. After I calmed down, I went back to the playground.

B2.text: This scene also reminds me of a park day when I fell badly enough to end a race. I was embarrassed as well as hurt, especially because everyone had seen it. After a short break, though, I returned to the game and the accident became a minor part of the day.
B2.grammarFocus: Past perfect + present perfect reflection + contrast

C1.text: One of my clearest park memories involves a fall that felt dramatic at the time. I scraped my knee, felt embarrassed in front of the other children, and briefly decided the entire afternoon was ruined. Within half an hour I was playing again. Looking back, the memory is a useful reminder of how quickly childhood disasters could expand and disappear.
C1.grammarFocus: Narrative stance + temporal layering + evaluative reflection

A2.text: When I was younger, I spent hours running outside. Now I usually exercise in a more planned way.

B2.text: This scene makes me compare childhood play with adult exercise. Running used to happen because a game required it; now movement is often planned, measured, or scheduled. I sometimes miss the feeling of being active without calling it exercise.

C1.text: The image highlights a change that is easy to overlook: as children, movement often emerges from play, curiosity, and social interaction, whereas adult activity is frequently structured around goals. I miss the unmeasured quality of childhood play—the fact that nobody needed to count the minutes or justify the effort.
C1.grammarFocus: Narrative stance + temporal layering + evaluative reflection
